title: Micaela Bastidas
summary: Wife of Túpac Amaru II, Bastidas ran the rebel administration at Tungasuca after the November 1780 uprising began, issuing safe-conduct passes and orders and coordinating attacks on other towns. She was arrested in April 1781 and executed in the Plaza de Armas of Cusco on 18 May 1781.

uncertainty.note: Birth is 23 June 1744 in Pampamarca per the Lienzo article; Encyclopedia.com gives 1745.

where.modern_name: Tungasuca, Túpac Amaru District, Canas Province, Cusco, Peru (pinned to the rebel seat she administered; born in Pampamarca, executed in Cusco)
where.historical_name: Tungasuca, rebel headquarters of Túpac Amaru II, 1780

importance.justification: Co-leader of the 1780-81 Andean uprising who managed supplies, passes and communications while Túpac Amaru was in the field.

audience_note: Mentions an execution by garrote; no graphic detail is given.

related.because: She led the rebel administration at Tungasuca during the uprising.

sources.title: Micaela Bastidas. Un fulgor que no cesa
sources.author: Sara Beatriz Guardia

reviewer_note: Birth year differs between sources (1744 versus 1745). Encyclopedia.com puts the rebel stronghold at San Felipe de Tungasuca. Pin is the village per OSM.
